summary: Defines an LDAP control that lets a client say copied information should not be used to answer, based on the X.511 dontUseCopy option. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: When you ask a librarian a question, you can insist on the original book, not a photocopy that might be old.

questions: what is the ldap dont use copy control
how do i force an authoritative ldap answer
subtitle: An LDAP request flag that says: answer from the original data, never from a copy.

tldr.problem: A directory server may answer from replicated or cached copies of entries, and a copy can be stale. Some clients need an authoritative answer.
tldr.mechanism: The Don't Use Copy control, a critical LDAP control with OID 1.3.6.1.1.22 and no value, is attached to a Compare or Search request. The server must use original (master) information or return a referral or an error.
tldr.outcome: Clients can insist on authoritative answers for the few checks that need them, at the cost of extra server work.

today: RFC 6171 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Background and Intended Use
sections.content:
RFC 6171 defines the Don't Use Copy control, an extension to the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). The control can be attached to request messages to say that copied (replicated or cached) information must not be used to provide service. It is based on the X.511 dontUseCopy service control option.

Without the control, the server is free to use copied, non-authoritative information. With it, the client requires that original (master) information be used.

The RFC gives an example: a client wants an authoritative answer to whether a user is a member of a group. It sends a compare request with the control, naming the group entry, the attribute member and the user's DN as the value.
sections.eli5: Most of the time a quick answer from a copy is fine. This control is a way to say, 'No, I want the real one,' for the rare questions where it matters.

sections.title: How the Control Works
sections.content:
The control is an LDAP control whose controlType is 1.3.6.1.1.22. The controlValue is absent, and the criticality MUST be TRUE. There is no corresponding response control.

It fits LDAP interrogation operations, namely Compare and Search. It is inappropriate for Abandon, Bind, Delete, Modify, ModifyDN, StartTLS and Unbind.

When the control is attached, the operation MUST NOT be performed on copied information. It MUST be performed on original information.

The RFC says the control is not meant for general use on all interrogation operations, only where needed for proper directory application behavior. Applications ought to be designed to use copied information well.
sections.eli5: It is a sticky note on your question that says 'original only, please.' The note has no extra words on it, and the server has to obey it.

sections.title: When the Original Is Not Available
sections.content:
If the original information for the target or base object is not available, either locally or through chaining, the server MUST either return a referral to a server believed to be better able to handle the request, or return an appropriate result code such as unwillingToPerform.

A referral does not necessarily point to the server holding the original information. An authoritative answer may also be unavailable to the client for various reasons.

If the client chases a referral given as an LDAP URL, it MUST send the control again on the request to the referred-to server. The RFC leaves the handling of other kinds of URIs to future specifications.
sections.eli5: If the librarian does not have the original book, they must say so or point you to someone who might. And when you go there, you have to ask for the original again.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Using the control may let an attacker perform or amplify a denial-of-service attack, because it can cause additional server resources to be used, for example when the server chooses to chain the request instead of returning a referral. Servers capable of chaining can mitigate this by limiting chaining to a particular group of authenticated entities.

LDAP is often used to store and distribute security-sensitive information such as access control and security policy. Failing to use the control may let an attacker gain unauthorized access by relying on stale data.
sections.eli5: Asking for originals costs the server more work, so a troublemaker could use that to slow it down. But trusting an old copy for something important can also let the wrong person in.

sections.title: Advertising Support and IANA
sections.content:
Servers implementing this specification SHOULD publish the object identifier 1.3.6.1.1.22 as a value of the supportedControl attribute in their root DSE. A server MAY advertise the extension only when the client is authorized to use it.

IANA has assigned the LDAP object identifier for the control and registered it as an LDAP protocol mechanism with usage Control, with RFC 6171 as the specification.
sections.eli5: A server can list the special requests it understands on a menu, and the control has its own official number so everyone recognises it.
